description: Natural Hazards Research Summit 2024: Potential for Mitigating Hurricane Wind Impact on Informally-Constructed Homes in Puerto Rico under Current and Future Climate Scenarios is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Amy Javernick-Will, University of Colorado Boulder (colorado.edu). This study investigates the resilience of informally-constructed light-frame timber houses in Puerto Rico, a region where households with limited resources face significant risks from climate hazards, notably hurricanes. This study conducts a component-based, performance-based wind engineering assessment of informally-constructed house typologies, defined based on extensive fieldwork, under both existing and projected future climate conditions. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-7jmq-q394. Keywords: Informally-constructed housing; Light frame timber houses; Hurricane hazard; Structural vulnerability; Climate change scenarios; Wind engineering. Published 2024-07-22. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
